workflow_sequence.description: User navigates to application and sees login screen
User submits login credentials (username and password)
Backend validates credentials against AccountSecurity table and generates bearer token

data_shape.query: SELECT account_id, password_hash FROM AccountSecurity WHERE username = ?

workflow_sequence.description: Backend returns authentication token and account details to frontend
Frontend stores token in localStorage and updates AuthContext
Frontend navigates to dashboard and requests transactions for logged-in account
Backend validates token, retrieves transactions where account is source or target

data_shape.query: SELECT * FROM Transactions WHERE source_account_id = ? OR target_account_id = ? ORDER BY transaction_date DESC, created_at DESC

workflow_sequence.description: Backend calculates running balance for account
Backend returns transactions and balance to frontend
Frontend displays transactions in TanStack Table with balance
User clicks 'Add Transaction' button to open form
User fills in transaction details (target account, amount, date) and submits
Backend validates transaction (sufficient funds, valid date, non-zero amount)
Backend creates transaction record in database
Backend returns created transaction to frontend
Frontend refreshes transaction list and balance
Frontend clears token from localStorage and AuthContext, redirects to login

instrumentation_events.description: Track transaction list views for usage analytics

contracts.name: Account
contracts.description: Represents a financial account in the system

columns: account_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
updated_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

contracts.name: Transaction
contracts.description: Represents a financial transaction between two accounts (immutable ledger)

columns: transaction_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
source_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES Accounts(account_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
target_account_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES Accounts(account_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

contracts.name: AccountSecurity
contracts.description: Stores authentication credentials and audit information (one-to-one with Account)

columns: security_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
account_id UUID NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES Accounts(account_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
created_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

contracts.name: POST /api/auth/login
contracts.description: Authenticate user and return bearer token

contracts.name: GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions
contracts.description: Retrieve all transactions for authenticated account

403.error: Forbidden - account ID does not match token

contracts.name: POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions
contracts.description: Create new transaction from authenticated account to target account

path_parameters.accountId: UUID (must match token account ID, becomes source_account_id)

request_body.date: ISO 8601 date string (required, must be today or past)

400.error: Amount must be non-zero | Future dates not allowed | Invalid date format | Target account is required

403.error: Forbidden - account ID does not match token

422.error: Insufficient funds | Target account not found

contracts.name: Client-side transaction display
contracts.description: Frontend retrieves all transactions in one call and handles sorting/display locally

added.rationale: No pagination required for 50-100 transactions. Simpler implementation, better UX (instant sorting), reduces server load
added.frontend_behavior: Fetch all transactions on dashboard load, sort locally using TanStack Table, no additional API calls for sorting
added.backend_behavior: Return all transactions for account in single response, sorted by date DESC
added.caching: Frontend can cache in TransactionContext, refresh on transaction creation or manual refresh

contracts.name: Real-time balance calculation
contracts.description: Backend calculates balance on-demand from transaction history

added.rationale: Balance is derived from transactions (functional alchemy). Real-time calculation ensures accuracy, no risk of stale cached balance
added.frontend_behavior: Display balance returned from API, no client-side calculation
added.backend_behavior: Calculate balance on each transaction list request: SUM(incoming) - SUM(outgoing)
added.optimization: If performance issues arise with 5,000-10,000 transactions, add materialized view or cached balance with invalidation on transaction creation

contracts.name: Token-based authentication
contracts.description: JWT bearer token scoped to account ID, stored in localStorage

added.rationale: Simple mock authentication, no session storage needed, token contains account ID for authorization
added.frontend_behavior: Store token in localStorage on login, include in Authorization header on all API calls, clear on logout
added.backend_behavior: Generate JWT with account ID claim on login, validate token signature and expiration on protected endpoints, extract account ID from token for authorization

architectural_decisions.decision: Use CQRS pattern with MediatR for backend API
architectural_decisions.justification: Separates read and write operations, provides clear separation of concerns, enables independent scaling of read/write paths, simplifies testing
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_BACKEND.md - established pattern for this application
architectural_decisions.impact: All API endpoints will use Command/Query handlers instead of direct controller logic

architectural_decisions.decision: Use Repository pattern for data access
architectural_decisions.justification: Abstracts database operations, enables mocking for unit tests, provides single point for query optimization
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_BACKEND.md - established pattern for this application
architectural_decisions.impact: All database access goes through ITransactionRepository, IAccountRepository, IAccountSecurityRepository interfaces

architectural_decisions.decision: Use React Context for state management (AuthContext, TransactionContext)
architectural_decisions.justification: Simple state management without global state library, co-located with components that use it, sufficient for application scope
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_UI.md - established pattern for this application
architectural_decisions.impact: No Redux or similar library needed, state management via hooks and context providers

architectural_decisions.decision: Use TanStack Table for transaction display
architectural_decisions.justification: Provides sortable columns, efficient rendering, extensible for future features (filtering, pagination)
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_UI.md - specified library for table display
architectural_decisions.impact: Transaction list will use TanStack Table component with column definitions

architectural_decisions.decision: Use shadcn/ui for all UI components
architectural_decisions.justification: Modern, accessible component library, consistent design system, TailwindCSS integration
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_UI.md - established UI library for this application
architectural_decisions.impact: All UI components (Button, Input, Card, Dialog, Form) will use shadcn/ui

architectural_decisions.decision: Store transactions with amount always positive, direction determined by source/target accounts
architectural_decisions.justification: Simplifies balance calculation, enforces data integrity at database level, aligns with double-entry bookkeeping principles
architectural_decisions.impact: Transaction amount is always > 0, CHECK constraint enforces this, balance calculated as incoming - outgoing

architectural_decisions.decision: Use UUID for all primary keys
architectural_decisions.justification: Enables distributed systems, avoids sequential ID enumeration attacks, supports future scaling
architectural_decisions.impact: All tables use UUID primary keys generated by database

architectural_decisions.decision: Implement immutable transaction ledger (no updates or deletes)
architectural_decisions.justification: Maintains audit trail, prevents data tampering, aligns with financial accounting principles
architectural_decisions.basis: app/docs/ARCHITECTURE_DATABASE.md and story requirement - established constraint
architectural_decisions.impact: No UPDATE or DELETE permissions on Transactions table, only INSERT allowed

architectural_decisions.decision: Calculate balance in real-time from transaction history
architectural_decisions.justification: Ensures accuracy, no risk of stale cached balance, sufficient performance for 50-100 transactions per account
architectural_decisions.basis: Functional alchemy principle - balance is derived property
architectural_decisions.impact: Balance calculated on each transaction list request, no separate balance column in Accounts table
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should the running balance be calculated in real-time or cached? - Answer: Real-time, with caching as future optimization if needed

architectural_decisions.decision: Use client-side sorting with single bulk fetch (no pagination)
architectural_decisions.justification: Simpler implementation, better UX (instant sorting), reduces server load, sufficient for 50-100 transactions
architectural_decisions.basis: Story requirement - no pagination in core app, display 50-100 transactions
architectural_decisions.impact: Frontend fetches all transactions in one call, sorts locally using TanStack Table

architectural_decisions.decision: Use JWT bearer tokens for authentication
architectural_decisions.justification: Stateless authentication, no server-side session storage needed, token contains account ID for authorization
architectural_decisions.impact: Backend generates JWT on login, frontend stores in localStorage, token included in Authorization header

architectural_decisions.decision: Set session timeout to 30 minutes of inactivity
architectural_decisions.justification: Balances security (prevents abandoned sessions) with UX (not too aggressive), industry standard for financial applications
architectural_decisions.basis: Industry best practice for financial applications
architectural_decisions.impact: JWT tokens expire after 30 minutes, frontend redirects to login on 401 response
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How long should user sessions last before expiring? - Answer: 30 minutes

architectural_decisions.justification: Standard precision for USD currency (2 decimal places), sufficient range for typical transactions
architectural_decisions.impact: All amounts stored with 2 decimal places, frontend formats as currency
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How should the system handle decimal precision for amounts? - Answer: 2 decimal places (DECIMAL(19, 2))

architectural_decisions.justification: Reasonable limit for personal banking, prevents data entry errors, aligns with edge case testing
architectural_decisions.basis: Edge case from story analysis - very large transaction amount
architectural_decisions.impact: Backend validates amount <= 1,000,000, frontend shows error if exceeded
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the maximum transaction amount allowed? - Answer: $1,000,000

architectural_decisions.decision: Set maximum payee name length to 500 characters
architectural_decisions.justification: Sufficient for any reasonable payee name, prevents abuse, aligns with edge case testing
architectural_decisions.basis: Edge case from story analysis - very long payee name
architectural_decisions.impact: Backend validates payee length <= 500, database schema allows VARCHAR(500) for payee if needed
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What is the maximum length for payee name? - Answer: 500 characters

architectural_decisions.decision: Use Intl.DateTimeFormat with en-US locale for date display
architectural_decisions.justification: Standard JavaScript internationalization API, consistent formatting, aligns with architecture examples
architectural_decisions.impact: Frontend formats dates as 'MMM DD, YYYY' (e.g., 'Jan 15, 2026')
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: What date format should be used for display? - Answer: en-US locale with Intl.DateTimeFormat

architectural_decisions.decision: Create mock data seeding script as separate tool in app/src/db
architectural_decisions.justification: Separates test data generation from application code, enables easy database reset for development/testing
architectural_decisions.impact: Seeding script creates 3-5 accounts with credentials and 100+ sample transactions
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: Should the mock data generation utility be part of the application or separate tool? - Answer: Separate seeding script

architectural_decisions.decision: Defer analytics sidecar integration until core app is functional
architectural_decisions.justification: Core transaction management is foundational, analytics is secondary, reduces initial complexity
architectural_decisions.basis: Story analysis recommendation - analytics is future enhancement
architectural_decisions.impact: Python analytics sidecar will be implemented after core app is working, integration points TBD
architectural_decisions.answers_open_question: How should the Python analytics sidecar integrate with the main application? - Answer: Deferred to future story

architectural_decisions.decision: Use composite indexes on (account_id, transaction_date DESC) for transaction queries
architectural_decisions.justification: Optimizes most common query pattern (transactions for account sorted by date), reduces query time for 5,000-10,000 transactions
architectural_decisions.impact: Database will have composite indexes on both source_account_id and target_account_id with date
